transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Lystera Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Lystera Platform), Olivia Ruiz (Lystera CTO)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Discussed POC capacity sizing and autoscale approach: reserved GPUs for baseline, burst pool for peaks, and model fallback policies for graceful degradation.
- Agreed on benchmark plan: 48-hour run across two model variants, capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, and cost metrics.
- Success criteria draft: p95 <= 350ms for short-completion paths, end-to-end 99% availability during business hours, and cost target below $X per 1M tokens (placeholder).
- Next steps: Redwood to send POC proposal and test harness; customer to provide traffic traces and quality eval set.

Topics: capacity sizing, reserved GPUs, burst strategy, fallback policies, KV cache, batching, benchmark plan, timelines

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)
00:00 - Evelyn: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Evelyn from Redwood, will do a quick intro and then Marco will go through the sizing suggestions.
00:18 - Olivia: Hi, thanks, Olivia here, short on time but wanted to make sure we cover the baseline and how this will fail over.
00:28 - Sara: Sara, yep, Head of ML, we own the evaluation and success criteria side.
00:33 - Tom: Tom, platform, I'll be giving traces and hooking up networking.
00:40 - Marco: Cool, thanks. quick agenda, we'll confirm workload shape, traffic peaks, latency SLOs, propose reserved vs burst, then benchmarks and timeline.
01:05 - Sara: Our main use case is real-time assistant in-product, typical requests are short 30-80 token prompts but we do have longer 300-800 token summarizations for nightly jobs. Peak QPS during business hrs is about 180 RPS, baseline trough 30 RPS, and we sometimes see sudden spikes up to 400 RPS during promotions.
01:32 - Evelyn: That's super helpful. Do you have token distribution for those requests?
01:38 - Tom: I can share a week's traces, roughly 70% short, 25% medium, 5% long. We'll upload to the shared folder after the call. Link: https://lystera.example.com/poctraces (placeholder)
01:58 - Marco: Based on that shape, for the POC we recommend a reserved pool sized to handle steady-state plus a moderate buffer, then a burst pool that can add capacity during spikes. For example, reserved GPUs enough for ~200 RPS steady throughput, then burst can add up to 8x capacity depending on limits.
02:25 - Sara: How does the burst work? is it cold starty, will there be latency penalty?
02:32 - Marco: Good question. There are two burst patterns: warm-burst (idle containers kept ready) and cold-burst (spin up new instances). Warm-burst reduces latency but increases baseline cost because you're keeping resources warm. Cold-burst is cheaper but incurs startup latency ~30-90s depending on model and infra. We generally recommend a hybrid: reserved capacity to cover p95 of normal peaks and warm-burst pool with thin instances for short spikes.
03:03 - Olivia: And fallback policies? we can't have the assistant go down in prod.
03:10 - Evelyn: We typically set multi-tier fallbacks: primary model on reserved GPUs, cheaper quantized variant on separate pool as fallback, and lastly an API-level degraded mode (e.g., truncated responses or simpler template replies). We can also route to a hosted Redwood-lite model if private capacity is exhausted.
03:32 - Tom: Is that what you call model-variant fallback? how's quality measured across that?
03:36 - Marco: Yes, model-variant fallback. Quality measured by the customer's eval set with automatic regression alerts. For the POC we'll run quality checks on a sample set of prompts before and after fallback to quantify delta.
03:52 - Evelyn: Quick note: we'll need the eval set or a subset from Sara to run the comparisons.
03:58 - Sara: Yeah, I'll prepare a 500 sample set with biz critical prompts.
04:05 - Evelyn: Perfect. Next let's talk numbers — you mentioned 180 RPS peak and 400 RPS spike. If we assume avg short request cost at X tokens, we estimate reserved capacity of 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state and a burst pool of 8 GPUs for spikes, that's a starting point.
04:29 - Tom: 4 GPUs? curious about how you arrived at that, what assumptions?
04:34 - Marco: We used the model latency profile, batching efficiency, and KV cache hit-rate. Assumption: batch size target 16 for short requests, KV cache hit roughly 30% for prefix reuse, and target p95 <= 350ms. For those we needed about 4 high-memory GPUs. This is preliminary — benchmark will validate.
05:02 - Sara: Batch size 16 — won't that add tail latency for interactive users?
05:08 - Marco: We do continuous batching and adaptive batching; for short requests the system keeps latency low by dynamically lowering batch sizes under latency pressure. So the 16 is an average. We can cap max batch size to control tail.
05:29 - Olivia: Can you explain KV cache effect? Tom: kv cash?
05:35 - Marco: (laughs) KV cache, yes — for chat-style sessions we keep key-value cache for recent tokens which speeds up generation for subsequent messages, reducing compute per request. If customers have repeated prefixes, we see big wins.
06:00 - Tom: On networking, we need VPC peering and SAML SSO for the control plane. Any blockers?
06:10 - Evelyn: We support VPC peering and customer-managed keys (KMS), plus SAML/SSO. We'll share security docs. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security (placeholder)
06:25 - Marco: Back to fallback: we recommend having a quantized variant (8-bit) preloaded into a separate reserved pool to handle unexpected sustained spikes. That keeps latency reasonable and cost lower than full fp16.
06:45 - Sara: For the POC can we set the quantized fallback as default for non-critical endpoints?
06:51 - Evelyn: Yes, route policies are configurable per-endpoint. For the POC we'll create two routes: 'assistant-critical' and 'assistant-degraded' with different model pins.
07:05 - Marco: On metrics we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue length, and cost per 1M tokens. Also error budgets and fallback counts.
07:20 - Sara: Success criteria idea: p95 under 400ms for critical endpoints, no more than 2% fallback events during business hours, and quality regression <2% measured on the eval set. Thoughts?
07:33 - Marco: Sounds reasonable for POC. We usually aim for p95 < 350ms but 400ms is OK as POC given your workload shape. We can try to optimize kernels if we need to push to 350.
07:50 - Olivia: Timelines — how fast can we stand up POC infra and run benchmarks?
07:55 - Evelyn: Post agreement, we can provision reserved pool within 48 hours, burst behavior and rollout policies configured same week. Benchmark scripts and canary can be ready in ~3 business days. So realistically start benchmarks around 2026-03-09 if deliverables align.
08:18 - Tom: We'll try to get traces and SSO in by 2026-03-06.
08:23 - Sara: What about cost estimation? need a rough monthly number to sign off.
08:28 - Marco: We'll provide two cost scenarios: conservative with warm-burst and lower-cost cold-burst scenario. POC pricing will be usage-based plus a short reserved commitment for the reserved pool. We'll include an example cost per 1M tokens given your token mix.
08:48 - Evelyn: Ok, let's talk benchmark design: 48-hour run, two model variants (full fp16 and quantized), traffic replay of your traces with synthetic spikes inserted, measure end-to-end latency and tail behavior. We'll also run targeted stress tests to exercise autoscaler limits.
09:10 - Sara: Will you run long jobs for the nightly summarization?
09:14 - Marco: Yes we'll include a nightly batch window, and measure throughput for long 300-800 token jobs; those are handled better by batching background workers, different autoscale policies. We'll size separate pools or priority classes for that.
09:32 - Tom: How do you handle GPU reservations and preemption?
09:36 - Marco: In Redwood Dedicated we do soft reservations plus burst on dedicated pools. For the POC we'll provision reserved GPUs that are not preemptible; burst may use preemptible nodes if customer agrees, with fallback to smaller model variant if preempted. We'll be explicit in the POC proposal about preemptible risk.
09:58 - Olivia: Network egress and data residency — we'll need logs to stay in EU region.
10:03 - Evelyn: We can pin the POC to the EU region and ensure audit logs are retained per your requirements. We'll include that in the security checklist.
10:15 - Sara: Any gotchas with quantization and hallucination changes?
10:20 - Marco: Quantization sometimes changes generation slightly; that's why the eval set is important. We report per-example deltas and false-positive/negative changes. For critical prompts we may pin not to fallback.
10:35 - Tom: For autoscaling thresholds, what signals do you use? GPU queue length, request latency, token inflight?
10:42 - Marco: We use a combination: queue length and request latency primarily, with token throughput as a secondary signal. For POC we'll surface recommended thresholds and tune during run.
11:00 - Evelyn: Ok, recap of concrete items: Redwood sends POC deck, security docs, pricing estimate; customer shares traces and eval set; Redwood runs 48-hour benchmark starting ~2026-03-09; follow-up canary run after benchmark.
11:18 - Sara: Agreed. Also need a control: can you provide a simple dashboard we can view during the run?
11:24 - Marco: Yes, Redwood Console will show per-route latency, token cost, and fallback counts. We'll give dashboard access.
11:32 - Olivia: On contract, are there minimum reserved commitments?
11:36 - Evelyn: For POC typically we do a short reserved term, week-to-week or month-to-month for the reserved pool; exact terms in proposal.
11:44 - Tom: Anything else around security testing? penetration?
11:48 - Evelyn: We can schedule a security review separately; we'll attach SOC2 summary, network architecture, and SAML docs in the packet.
11:56 - Sara: One more question: how deterministic are the kernels and perf across different hosts? we saw variance with another vendor.
12:03 - Marco: We have per-GPU optimized kernels and we report performance variance in the benchmark. For POC we'll run multiple runs to estimate variance and surface 95% confidence.
12:20 - Olivia: Great. If we get the traces over the next few days we can be on track for the 9th.
12:27 - Evelyn: Awesome. I'll follow up with the proposal and a shared folder for artifact uploads.
12:33 - Tom: I'll upload traces and infra contacts.
12:36 - Sara: I'll finalize the eval prompts and success criteria doc.
12:40 - Evelyn: Thanks everyone. We'll capture these action items and circle back.
12:46 - Marco: Quick note, during the benchmark we'll also test fallback rates by artificially draining reserved capacity to ensure routing policies behave as expected.
12:56 - Olivia: Thanks, talk soon.
13:00 - (call ends)

Notes and references:
